newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity mostly eases on Palo nuke boost.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity mostly eases on Palo nuke boost.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading mostly lower Wednesday following news an Arizona nuclear generation unit was increasing power after a Tuesday reduction, industry sources said.

The futures front months traded mostly higher Wednesday morning on news the 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Palo Verde nuclear plant near Phoenix, Ariz., had cut power to 60 percent overnight to repair re-heater tubes.
However, a spokesman for the plant said Wednesday that unit 2 was in the process of ramping back up to full power following repairs.
"We spiked early today based on the 60 percent (at Palo Verde 2), but we seem to have settled down to a little more stable levels right now," said one power futures broker.

As of 1230 EDT July PV was trading up 15 cents at $33.50 following exchanges in a range of $33.20-33.75 per megawatt hour (MWh), while August PV was down 50 cents at $34.35 after trades in a range of $34.20-34.90 per MWh.
July California Oregon Border (COB) was down 26 cents at $20.60 after exchanges in a range of $20.50-20.95, while August was down 60 cents at $23.30 following trades at $23.10-23.90 per MWh.
Both the July PV and COB contracts expire today.
NYMEX said as of 1145 EDT an estimated total of 146 COB and 217 PV contracts had traded.
As of 1225 EDT, July Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 0.6 cents at $2.28 per million British thermal units.
Some support for the electricity contracts was also seen from talk of the timing of a restart of the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state, market sources said.
Restart of WNP-2 may be pushed beyond expectations of later this week, as the unit still requires Nuclear Regulatory Commission approval to resume operations.
Meanwhile, Bonneville Power Administration, which markets WNP-2's power production, has said it hopes the unit will resume output late next week.
Meteorologists called for temperatures in the Northwest to run below early summer norms through next week, while those in the Southwest would average mostly near to above normal.
COB open interest for June 24 fell 100 to 6,803 while PV open interest fell 104 to 6,357, NYMEX said.
